Neha Joshi is a 24-year-old primary school teacher who loves storytelling.

An elephant named Mubarak lived in the forest. Every morning, he watched the other animals go about their business and scold them for walking too fast or chewing gum. One day, a small mouse named Tina came to him with a tiny piece of gum stuck between her teeth. "I can help you," she said. The two were friends, and they walked together every day.
One afternoon, Tina found a big pile of gum under a tree. She had never seen it before. "This is mine!" she called. An elephant named Mr. Bunny heard her call and stopped. He looked at his ears. Then he smiled and gave Mubarak one more piece of gum. They both laughed. From that day on, they walked side by side, and Mubarak was not afraid anymore.

The family's car broke down on the highway at night. The driver, Mr. Das, had to go through a narrow path and could not see them. He stopped for a moment and looked up. A small girl named Lakshmi was standing in front of her window with a bag of rice. "I have something," she said. She took out an old tin can from her pocket. It held two buckets of water. "Take it." They drank together, laughing as they drove home.

The little moon was so tired that she could not sleep. She lay on the floor and watched the stars, wishing they would come out one after another. One night, a tiny voice came from behind her, "I am tired too." The moon looked down at her with big eyes. Then it spoke. It said, "Thank you for being here, but I will be up soon." The little moon smiled and went to bed slowly.

Every morning, Aarav climbed the roof of her village to find a kite. He searched every corner and found nothing. One day, he saw a big red kite stuck in a tree. "I will get it," he said.
He ran down the hill with his hands full of kites. The wind blew them away. A small girl named Lakshmi caught one on her head. She looked up at him with wide eyes. "Thank you!" she said.
Aarav smiled and flew the kite high above the house. Every evening after that, he brought it back for Lakshmi's family. They sat under the old tree and watched the sunset together.

Rohan had a secret room in his house, and every night he heard strange noises. One evening, the doorbell rang again, and it sounded like something was about to happen. He sat down on the floor with his head in his hands and closed his eyes. The noise came slowly. Then he opened them all. A tiny voice said, "I am here." Rohan could not believe it. It was a small silver box that glowed softly at once. Inside were stories of happy children who played together every day. When the bell rang again, he opened the doors one by one.

The puppy, named Pippa, walked into the school gate every day after lunch. The teacher said it was time to go home. But Pippa did not listen. She sat on a bench and watched the children walk by. One afternoon, her friend Tara came over with a bag of biscuits. "Pippa," she whispered, "I have something for you."

She handed him one. He wagged his tail, then ran off to play in the yard. Pippa chased him around the block, but he always stayed near her side. When she returned, she gave him a big hug.

That evening, they went back to class together. Pippa sat on the bench, watching the children, feeling safe and warm.

Rohan was cooking dinner when his mother came in and said, "I'm making a little rice. Could you make it for me?" Rohan looked at her with big eyes. She nodded and gave him the rice she had given him. He ate it all. When he left, his hands were cold, but he did not mind. His father laughed and said, "You are doing well." Then they sat down to eat together.

Goldie the goldfish was a very small fish. She wanted to see the world, but she knew no one would come near her. One day, a little girl named Lily came along and saw her. "Hello," said Lily.
"Would you like some of my soup?" asked Goldie.

"Yes!" cried Lily. They sat on the grass together, and Lily gave Goldie a warm bowl. The soup smelled delicious. Soon, they were both laughing and talking.
Lily's mother called them home that evening. That night, they ate dinner with a big plate of rice and a soft blanket. From then on, every time Goldie swam in the sea, she felt happy and free.

Every morning, the tiffin box sat in his bag all by itself. It was empty. His mother had no money and nobody knew where to find it.

One day, he found a tiny green one under his shirt. He held it up with both hands. "I have lost my lunch," he said.

His mother looked at him. She smiled and took him back inside. The box stayed there, still full of food for the next morning.

The parrot, Tiku the parakeet, had never spoken to anyone. When his owner, Mr. Rao, left him on a bench in the village, he stopped and said quietly that he would not talk again for two days.

"I am sorry," he said. "But I will stay away from you."

Mr. Rao looked at the bird closely. Then he smiled. He picked up the cage and put it back where he found it.

Tiku sat on the grass with her head tucked under his arm. She did not move. After three days she sang a soft song of thanks.

Grandfather Mehta had been teaching his granddaughter to ride a bicycle for years, and she was always tired. One morning, her mother gave him a small bike with two wheels and a bell. Grandpa stood at the doorway, watching from the sofa. "You are doing well," he said. But when he tried to pedal, the wheel slipped off his foot and rolled under the seat. The bell rang loudly. Grandma looked worried. She took out her phone and called an adult right away. They fixed it together, and Grandpa rode on the bicycle every day after that.

When the train finally stopped at her door, she sat on a bench and watched. Her shoes were wet from the rain last night, and her bag was empty. She looked around, but there was no train. Then she remembered that her cousin had made a funny face out of nothing. "Maybe it's dry," she said. The next day, she went to look for something else. On the second day, she found a small box with a note: "I miss you too." It read, "Dear Diya, I missed you both when we ran away together." They hugged, and she promised never to forget them again.

The monkey and the crocodile lived in a big pond. They were friends, but one day, a little girl named Sana came to the pond with her mother.

"Crocodiles are very strong," she said. "But I will not let you go."

Sana was scared of them at first. But then she saw how much they ate. She sat on a rock and watched. The crocodile looked down and smiled. He walked slowly up the bank, looking for his own way back into the water.

When he found it, he jumped out and roared loudly. Sana gasped. Then she laughed and clapped.

They stayed together until the sun went down.

The snake and the ants lived in a big garden. The ant was very small, but he could climb on the leaves. One day, a bee buzzed near him. "Where are you going?" asked the bee.
"To find food," said the snake. He had never been so far from home before.

One hot afternoon, the bee flew away. The snake followed it. But the bee stayed behind a bush, and the ant felt scared. Then he saw something shiny under a leaf. It was a tiny nest with eggs inside.

He climbed down carefully. Inside were 3 baby ants: one for each of them. They looked just as happy to be together as if they belonged.

The bee thanked him and flew off into the sky.

The lion was the king of the jungle, and his job was to build houses for the animals. One day, a monkey named Tiku climbed onto the roofs of a house in Kerala.

"I want to make my own room," he said. "But I have no tools."

Tiku looked around. He found a stick, some leaves from a nearby tree, and a small shovel. He dug a deep hole with all his might.

He covered it with soil. Then he added a few more sticks. The top of the hole became a little doorway.

When he finished, the whole room glowed like a tiny lamp. Tiku stepped out, grinning, and carried on.

A jackal named Kaku lived in the jungle. Every morning, he walked to the river and sat on a rock. He was very big and strong.

One day, a little girl named Sita saw him standing alone by the water. She wanted to be his queen. "I will help you," she said.

Kaku roared. The other animals ran away when they heard her call. But one night, a small mouse named Tikkun hopped onto the rock and started to eat the leaves.

Sita stopped. Then she remembered that her father had told her about being king of the jungle. So she stood up and roared as loud as she could.
The lion woke up and shook off all the fear. He thanked her for helping him and gave her a golden crown.

Hanuman was a brave and wise king who had to cross the sea alone. He walked slowly, holding his chariot with both hands. The waves were strong, but he stayed calm.

One day, a storm came and washed away all of Lanka's land. Hanuman stopped and looked at it for a moment. Then he saw that the sea was far from where he wanted to go. It lay in a deep hole, and nobody could reach him there.

He took out his charioteer and set off on foot. The wind carried him along, and by the end of the year, he reached Lanka safely.

Arjuna was a very tall bird who lived in the forest. One morning, he saw a small green bird with big eyes and sharp beak. "What are you doing?" asked Arjuna.
"I'm looking for food," said the tiny bird.

So they went to find it together. They looked under leaves, behind trees and even inside bushes. At last, they found a nest of eggs on a rocky branch. The bird flew away, but her bright eyes showed that she had seen everything.

Pooja sat down beside him and listened. She told him about how birds look at things from above, so he could see their colours too. He learned that his own eye is special because it sees far more than anyone else's does.

Alice fell down the rabbit hole and scraped her knee. She cried, but then she remembered that her mother had told her to stay calm when danger came near.

"I'm fine," said Alice's mother. "But I want you to be safe."

She picked up a stick and held it out for the rabbit. The rabbit hopped away slowly. When she reached the other side of the tunnel, Alice was standing there with her knee still. Her mother looked at her and sighed. Then she took her hand and led her back into the dark.

The next day, Alice followed her mother's lead straight through the tunnel safely.

Every morning, the puppy walked into her school yard with a small red tag. She held it in her mouth and ran to tell her teacher.
One day, she was walking alone when she heard a mew outside the gate. The puppy had run away! She stopped and looked at him. He was white and fluffy, with big ears. "You are so soft," he said.

"Thank you!" she said.

The next day, she brought the puppy back inside. Her mother hugged her and told her that the puppy belonged with them both.

Every evening, the park guard let a boy drop his red ball. He was only three years old and had no money to buy it. His friends laughed at him.

One day, a girl named Ananya came up with an idea. She said she could lend him her red ball if he gave her one more coin each. The next morning, they walked together to the park gate.

The ball rolled over the grass. It landed in a pond, where a small fish swam out. Ananya's face lit up.

She picked it up gently. Then she dropped it into the water.

A man who worked there saw what happened. He took it back from the children and thanked them for lending it.

Buena the small bird lived in a cage on a balcony. Every day, he watched the other birds fly above him and then flap their wings to catch his breath.

One morning, Buena opened her cage door and saw a little girl named Lina standing outside with a bag of seeds. "Can you help me?" she asked.

"Of course," said Buena. He flew over and landed gently on her shoulder. She laughed so hard that she forgot about her bag.

From then on, Buena was never alone. Whenever he wanted something, he would flick through the window and look at it. The wind blew softly around him, and even his feathers looked beautiful.

Every morning, the two of them sat together at the table and shared their lunch. They ate with each other's hands in a circle, and they talked about what they liked to eat. One day, the teacher said that two friends had different tastes. The class went silent for an hour. Then one afternoon, a boy named Raju came up from his Class 4 building and asked if he could have half of the sandwich. He was shy but polite. "Thank you," he said. "I am sorry." Raju smiled and gave him half.

The cat, named Tukku, lived in a small house with her owner, Mr. Kapoor. Every evening, the rain came down hard and made him shiver.

One day, he heard a tiny voice from outside his window. It was a little kitten named Pipi who had fallen out of bed. "Please don't fall," she said.

"I'm scared," said Tukku.

Mr. Kapoor smiled. He put on his raincoat and held out her paws. The kitten climbed onto his lap and sat there, feeling safe.

Together, they watched the rain slowly turn into soft green clouds. After that, the rain did not bother them at all.
